From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Monthly Close - Line Item Inquiry

Gabriel, Victor,

In reviewing the monthly close package, I need clarification on the line item under 'Other Operating Expenses' – specifically the entry for $48,200 in 'Miscellaneous Fees.' This is not matching my records for the period.

Could you provide a breakdown of what this covers? If it's an accrual or a vendor charge, please confirm the invoice or reference number. I need this resolved before we finalize the close.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, Kestrel Manufacturing

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Monthly Close - Line Item Inquiry

Hi Dana,

Thanks for flagging this. I can confirm the $48,200 entry under 'Miscellaneous Fees' in Other Operating Expenses is an accrual—not a vendor charge or one-off write-off.

The breakdown is as follows:
- Approximately $46,000 relates to the September supplier invoicing timing lag we discussed (the September invoices that landed after the close cut, rebooked per our accrual policy). This overstates Q3 COGS slightly and is the main driver of the 2.3% margin swing versus Q2.
- The remaining ~$2,200 is a late June vendor rebate credit that posted after the statements cut and was rebooked into June per policy. That one is documented in the close folder—you may not have seen the note yet.

I've placed the supporting documentation (invoice references and calculation sheet) in the shared drive. Happy to walk you through the details before Thursday if that helps.

Best regards,
Gabriel Fontes

From: Victor Alade
To: Dana Whitfield

Dana,

To close this out cleanly:

- The $46,000 accrual is fully offset when the September invoices post in October—no residual in Q4. The October entry reverses the accrual against actuals, so you won't need to track anything beyond that.
- The $2,200 vendor rebate reference is in the close folder (document 'Jun_Rebate_REF_2200.pdf'), matching AP ledger line 1043. Yes, it was booked into June per our accrual policy; the vendor's fiscal calendar doesn't affect our rebooking cut.
- September invoices total exactly $46,000 (no rounding). Breakdown: INV-22101 ($18,400), INV-22108 ($14,750), INV-22115 ($12,850). All cross-referenced in the calculation sheet.

I've also confirmed there are no write-offs or reclassifications in COGS this quarter—the margin swing is entirely raw material cost increases plus the $46k timing lag, which flows into Q4 as approved.

If you want a quick walkthrough Wednesday afternoon before Thursday's board review, I'm free 2-4 PM. Otherwise, happy to review the final deck once you've updated it.

Best,
Victor Alade
Tax Manager

I've verified the invoice dates against our AP system, and all three post by the second week of October. You can close the close without any Q4 tracking on this item.

2. Invoice references and exact amounts (now cross-referenced in the calculation sheet in the shared drive under the close folder):
   - September accrual: $46,000 exactly, split across INV-22101 ($21,400), INV-22102 ($14,800), and INV-22103 ($9,800). No rounding or additional charges.
   - June rebate credit: $2,200 exactly, reference REB-88421. Confirmed it was rebooked into June per our accrual policy—the vendor's fiscal calendar doesn't affect our rebooking cut.

I've also added a note in the close folder flagging the rebate timing rationale, so the audit trail is clean.

Both items are locked in the documentation, so you should have everything you need to finalize. Happy to jump on a quick call Wednesday afternoon if that helps—otherwise, I'm comfortable moving forward with Thursday's close.

Best regards,
